title: Ksp expression for dissolution of a salt A_aB_b(s)

items.label: K_{sp}
items.meaning: solubility-product constant for the dissolution A_aB_b(s) ⇌ aA^{m+}(aq) + bB^{n-}(aq); unitless in AP use

items.label: [\mathrm{A}^{m+}]
items.meaning: equilibrium molar concentration of the cation (mol/L)

items.label: m
items.meaning: magnitude of the cation charge

items.label: a
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of the cation, which becomes its exponent

items.label: [\mathrm{B}^{n-}]
items.meaning: equilibrium molar concentration of the anion (mol/L)

items.label: n
items.meaning: magnitude of the anion charge

items.label: b
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of the anion, which becomes its exponent

caution: The solid salt is left out of the expression (7.3.A.2). Use square brackets for concentrations, and raise each ion's concentration to its coefficient in the balanced dissolution equation. When Q is written in this form, the comparison to Ksp predicts precipitation (Q > Ksp).

title: Equilibrium expression Kc (and Qc) for aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD

items.label: K_c
items.meaning: equilibrium constant in terms of concentrations (Qc has the same form, using concentrations at any time)

items.label: [\mathrm{C}]
items.meaning: molar concentration of product C (mol/L)

items.label: c
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of C, used as its exponent

items.label: [\mathrm{D}]
items.meaning: molar concentration of product D (mol/L)

items.label: d
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of D, used as its exponent

items.label: [\mathrm{A}]
items.meaning: molar concentration of reactant A (mol/L)

items.label: a
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of A, used as its exponent

items.label: [\mathrm{B}]
items.meaning: molar concentration of reactant B (mol/L)

items.label: b
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of B, used as its exponent

caution: Kc = Qc only at equilibrium. Substances whose concentrations are independent of amount (solids and pure liquids) are not included. For gas-phase reactions, the Kp and Qp form uses partial pressures. Pay attention to whether Kc or Kp is asked for; conversion between them is not assessed.
ced_evidence: 7.3.A.1 "the law of mass action indicates that the equilibrium expression for (Kc, Qc)"

title: K for a reversed reaction

items.label: K_{\text{reverse}}
items.meaning: equilibrium constant for the reaction written in the reverse direction

items.label: K_{\text{forward}}
items.meaning: equilibrium constant for the original reaction as written

caution: The same algebraic manipulation applies to Q, since K and Q have identical mathematical forms (7.6.A.4).
ced_evidence: 7.6.A.1 "When a reaction is reversed, K is inverted."

title: K for summed reactions

items.label: K_{\text{overall}}
items.meaning: equilibrium constant of the overall reaction obtained by adding the individual reactions

items.label: K_1
items.meaning: equilibrium constant of the first reaction in the sum

items.label: K_2
items.meaning: equilibrium constant of the second reaction in the sum

caution: K values multiply (they do not add) when reactions are added. For more than two steps, multiply all the K values. The same manipulation applies to Q (7.6.A.4).
ced_evidence: 7.6.A.3 "the K of the resulting overall reaction is the product of the K's"

title: K when coefficients are multiplied by c

items.label: K_{\text{new}}
items.meaning: equilibrium constant for the reaction after all stoichiometric coefficients are multiplied by c

items.label: K
items.meaning: equilibrium constant for the original reaction

items.label: c
items.meaning: factor by which every stoichiometric coefficient is multiplied; it becomes the exponent on K

caution: Multiplying the coefficients by c raises K to the power c; it does not multiply K by c. The same manipulation applies to Q (7.6.A.4).
ced_evidence: 7.6.A.2 "multiplied by a factor c, K is raised to the power c"
